# One tree's share of the secret-scan allow-list:
#
#     path | rule-id | sha256 fingerprint | reason
#
# The format, what an entry may say, and why this is a directory rather than a
# file are argued once in README.md beside this file. Do not restate them here.
#
# covers: tools/


# The scaffold's own suite.
#
# tools/new-service renders a service's Compose unit and writes the entries
# its literals owe; its suite pins what that render produces, which puts the
# rendered broker account in the suite as well.

tools/new-service/test_new_service.py | credential-assignment | 1c47d06cedb2 | The scaffold suite pinning the per-service broker account it renders into compose.
tools/new-service/test_new_service.py | connection-string-password | 19b974097990 | The scaffold suite pinning the per-service Redis user it renders into compose.


# The dead-letter tool.
#
# tools/dead-letters reads the operator's credential from a curl config or the
# environment, never from argv; the lines below name a password and hold none.

tools/dead-letters/dead_letters.py | connection-string-password | 723340c8c4c1 | Splitting the curl config's user line into name and password; the value is read, not written.
tools/dead-letters/dead_letters.py | connection-string-password | 6aea782b50b2 | Reading the password from the environment; no value is in the source.
tools/dead-letters/dead_letters.py | connection-string-password | 32d7d6181dbe | Unpacking the loaded credential; no value is in the source.
tools/dead-letters/test_dead_letters.py | credential-assignment | da3fd0c5abaa | A placeholder the suite's in-memory broker never checks; no broker ever reads it.
